title: God’s Purpose in Pain
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: God’s purpose in pain means that the Lord can work through suffering without calling evil good or minimizing hurt. Pain is not meaningless in God’s hands, even when His purposes are hidden.
summary: God’s purpose in pain means that the Lord can work through suffering without calling evil good or minimizing hurt. Pain is not meaningless in God’s hands, even when His purposes are hidden.
christFocus: Jesus Christ shows that God can accomplish redemption through suffering. The cross was evil committed by sinners, yet God used it to bring salvation and glory.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God’s purpose in pain must be handled carefully. Scripture does not teach that evil itself is good or that sufferers should pretend pain does not hurt.

At the same time, Scripture teaches that God is sovereign over suffering and can work through it for good. Joseph’s suffering, Christ’s cross, and the trials of believers all show that God’s purposes can be deeper than what is visible.

God may use pain to refine faith, produce endurance, expose idols, deepen compassion, strengthen hope, or open doors for witness. His work does not erase grief, but it gives suffering a larger frame.

The greatest example is the cross. Human evil and injustice were real, yet God accomplished salvation through the suffering of Christ. This anchors hope when believers cannot understand their own pain.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often swing between two errors: saying pain has no meaning, or carelessly assigning specific reasons to suffering. This doctrine gives humility and hope.

It helps believers trust God without pretending to know everything He is doing. His purposes are wise, even when hidden, and His goodness is proven in Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not rush to explain every pain. Trust God’s character, bring sorrow honestly to Him, and ask how He may be forming faithfulness in you. When helping others, avoid careless explanations; point them to the God who worked redemption through the cross.
